title: Family
theme: Siblings, parents visiting, a family dinner, a disagreement, looking after someone.

storylets.title: A parent at the door with a pot
storylets.note: A parent arrives carrying food. A hug on the step. The relation is stated at the door and that is all.

A.desc: an adult at their own door

b1: {B.desc} comes up to {place} with a covered pot held in both hands.
{B.desc} arrives at the door carrying a heavy pot wrapped in a cloth, the lid rattling.
{B.desc} walks up slowly, a lidded pot held out in front.
b2: The door slides open. {A} and {B.desc} embrace outside, the pot held out to one side.
{A} steps out and hugs {B.desc}. It goes on for a while.
{B.desc} hugs {A} in the doorway and pats {A.his} back.
b3: Both go into {place} with the pot, and the door slides shut.
{A} takes the pot and holds the door. {B.desc} goes in first.
{B.desc} goes through the door with {A} close behind.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "{B.addr}, you did not have to carry all that up."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "A {B.rel} worries. Eat something."
Overheard: {B.desc} says to {A}: "Eat. You are too thin. I brought enough for the week."
Overheard: {B.desc} says to {A}: "Everyone back home asks after you. Call more often."
Overheard: {A} asks: "Did the others come? No? Next time, then."

storylets.title: Noodles with a sibling
storylets.note: Two siblings share a stall counter. Shows a recurring pair without naming them.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} come across the square side by side, trading shoves.
{A} falls in beside {B.desc} on the way to the stalls.
{B.desc} and {A} arrive together, arguing over where to eat.
b2: {A} and {B.desc} reach the counter. {A} orders for both without asking.
{B.desc} leans on the counter and orders. {A} adds a second bowl.
At the stall, {A} and {B.desc} point at different pictures and settle on one.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} eat in silence until {B.desc} steals a bite out of {A.his} bowl.
{B.desc} laughs at something and nearly spills the broth. {A} slides a napkin across.
{A} and {B.desc} sit on neighboring stools, elbows touching, bowls steaming.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "You always did steal my food. Some {B.rel} you are."
Overheard: {B.desc} tells {A}: "The folks say you never call. So your {B.rel} is calling in person."

storylets.title: Groceries for an older relative
storylets.note: A younger person carries shopping to an elder's door.

A.desc: an adult with a sack of shopping

B.desc: an older relative at a door

b1: {A} comes up to {place} with a full sack of groceries in both arms.
{A} brings a loaded sack up to the door and knocks with a knuckle.
{A} arrives at the door with a paper sack, hip against the rail.
b2: The door slides open. {A} hands the sack to {B.desc}.
{A} holds out the groceries. {B.desc} takes them with both hands and checks inside.
{A} hands over the sack, a folded receipt and the change. {B.desc} counts the coins.
b3: {B.desc} talks at length from the doorway. {A} nods through all of it.
{A} and {B.desc} chat outside {place}. {B.desc} wags a finger at one point.
{B.desc} presses something into {A.his} palm. {A} tries to give it back and fails.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Eat the greens first, {B.addr}. I counted the cans."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "What would I do without my {A.rel}?"
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Thank you, child. You always did carry more than you should."

storylets.title: A walk with a grown child
storylets.note: A parent and an adult son or daughter on the square. Plain texture.

A.desc: a parent out walking with a grown child

b1: {A} crosses the square with {B.desc}, the two of them in step.
{A} and {B.desc} come along the sidewalk, {B.desc} carrying both bags.
{B.desc} walks on the outside of the sidewalk, half a pace ahead of {A}.
b2: {A} stops at the edge of the pond and {B.desc} leans over to look at the koi.
{A} stands with {B.desc} at the water. {B.desc} points at something.
{A} and {B.desc} linger by a planter. {A} straightens {B.his} collar, and {B.desc} lets it happen.
b3: {B.desc} lifts a hand to someone leaving the stalls.
{B.desc} waves at a figure across the square, then lowers the hand.
{B.desc} gives a quick wave to someone by the vending machines.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "{A.addr}, sit a minute. You've been on your feet all day."
Overheard: {A} says: "Look at my {B.rel}, all grown up and still letting me fuss."

storylets.title: A raised voice on the sidewalk
storylets.note: Siblings argue in public. Chain: fam.cold-shoulder, then fam.apology-hug, or it fizzles.

b1: {A} and {B.desc} stand face to face and argue, hands moving.
Raised voices on the sidewalk. {A} jabs a finger at {B.desc}, who steps back.
{A} and {B.desc} argue by the rail. Two walkers cross to the other side.
b2: {A} turns away, then back, then away again.
{A} shrugs once and stares at the ground.
{A} shakes {A.his} head and turns away.
b3: {B.desc} leaves in the other direction, fast.
{B.desc} storms off toward the corner without a look back.
{B.desc} walks away, shoulders up.

log: Overheard: {A} shouts: "You always do this! You said you'd take her this time!"
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "And you always make me the bad one. Ask anyone, they'll tell you."
Overheard: {A} says: "Don't use that tone with me. I'm your {A.rel}."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Being my {A.rel} doesn't make it your place to decide."

storylets.title: Passing without a word
storylets.note: After the quarrel, two siblings cross paths and say nothing. Observed only.

b1: {A} cuts across the square, eyes front.
{A} walks along the block, a bag over one shoulder.
{A} heads for the corner at a steady pace.
b2: {B.desc} comes the other way, eyes on a comm.
{B.desc} turns into the same stretch from a side street.
{B.desc} crosses the path ahead, looking at nothing.
b3: The two pass at arm's length. Neither looks. {A} turns away at the corner.
{A} shakes {A.his} head once after {B.desc} has gone.
{A} and {B.desc} pass without a word and keep going.

storylets.title: Meeting halfway
storylets.note: Pays off the quarrel. One sibling holds out a hand, then a hug. Never forced.

A.desc: an adult waiting on a bench

b1: {A} sits on a bench and turns a cup in both hands.
{A} takes a seat on the bench and stares across the square.
{A} perches on the edge of the bench, knee bouncing.
b2: {B.desc} comes across the square slowly, hands in pockets.
{B.desc} approaches the bench and stops two steps short.
{B.desc} walks up and stands a pace from the bench.
b3: {A} stands. A few words. Then {A} and {B.desc} hug, rocking a little.
{A} gets up and says something short. {B.desc} nods, and they hug on the spot.
{B.desc} holds out a hand. {A} takes it, stands, and pulls {B.desc} into a hug.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "I'm sorry I said it like that. I was out of line."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Me too. Let's not do that again. Come eat."

storylets.title: Calling home from a bench
storylets.note: A phone call to family. Only one side is heard.

b1: {A} sits on a bench and takes out a comm.
{A} takes a seat and thumbs a contact open.
{A} perches on the edge of the bench, comm in a fist.
b2: {A} talks on the comm and smiles now and then. Mostly listens.
{A} holds the comm to one ear and rubs the back of {A.his} neck.
{A} talks softly into the comm and nods at nothing.

log: Comm, one side: {A} says: "Yes, I ate. Yes, I'm wearing the jacket."
Comm, one side: {A} says: "Tell everyone I'll be there Sunday. Save me the good chair."
Comm, one side: {A} says: "How is everyone? Put them all on for a second."

storylets.title: Sharing a bench with an elder
storylets.note: A senior and a younger relative sit. A snack changes hands.

A.desc: a young adult on a bench

b1: {A} and {B.desc} sit on a bench and watch the foot traffic.
{B.desc} lowers {B.him}self onto a bench with {A} close by.
{A} takes a seat next to {B.desc}. Neither speaks yet.
b2: {B.desc} hands {A} a wrapped sweet from a pocket.
{B.desc} passes {A} half a bun, wrapped in paper.
{B.desc} holds out a small tin. {A} takes one and nods.
b3: {B.desc} talks and talks. {A} nods in the right places.
{A} listens with an elbow on a knee while {B.desc} points down the block.
{B.desc} tells a story with both hands. {A} laughs once.

log: Overheard: {A} tells {B.desc}: "{B.addr}, you've told me that one."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Humor your old {B.rel}. Listen."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "When I was your age, I would not sit still either."

storylets.title: A bag, a drop-off, a hug
storylets.note: A relative arrives in the city. The player may see the arrival; the settling in arrives as hearsay.

b1: {A} steps off a drop-off lift with a battered bag over one shoulder.
{A} rides the lift down with one bag, looks up at the towers, and waits.
{A} arrives at the drop-off alone, a coat over {A.his} arm and a bag at {A.his} feet.
b2: {B.desc} jogs up. {A} and {B.desc} hug, bag swinging.
{B.desc} spots {A} and waves. They embrace at the foot of the lift.
{A} and {B.desc} hug, then hold each other at arm's length.
b3: {A} and {B.desc} head off together, {B.desc} carrying the bag.
{B.desc} takes the bag and walks {A} toward the street.
{A} and {B.desc} walk off side by side, talking fast.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Cousin! Look at you. You can have my couch as long as you need."
Overheard: {A} says: "Your favorite {A.rel} made it. This bag is mostly food from home."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} came in on the lift last week, a cousin of someone on the block.
Overheard: {S} says to {L}: "A new face at the lift. {A.desc}. Came with one bag."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} just got to the city and is staying with relatives.
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} is new to the district and has been seen at the stalls.
entry: Arrived in the city last week (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Came in on the lift with one bag, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Moved to the district from elsewhere, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: Knocking on a door that stays shut
storylets.note: A parent comes and nobody opens. Observed outcome only. Pairs with an estrangement that happens off screen.

B.desc: an older visitor at the door

b1: {B.desc} knocks on the door, a small parcel under one arm. Three taps, a pause, three more.
{B.desc} raps on the door of {place} with a parcel in the other hand and steps back to wait.
{B.desc} knocks and calls through the panel, a small parcel held against {B.his} chest.
b2: {B.desc} stands outside {place}, the parcel held in both hands.
{B.desc} stays at the door for {n} minutes. Nobody opens.
{B.desc} waits, leans on the rail, waits.
b3: {B.desc} sets the parcel by the door and leaves.
{B.desc} leaves with the parcel still in hand.
{B.desc} turns away from {place} and walks off slowly.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} calls through the door: "It's your {B.rel}. I only want to leave this. Open up."
Overheard: {B.desc} calls: "Your {B.rel} came all this way. One minute."
Overheard: {B.desc} calls: "Please, just a word. I'm not asking to come in."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} has stopped speaking to the family. The door stays shut when they visit.
Overheard: {S} says to {L}: "{A.desc} won't open the door to {A.his} own parent. Not a word of why."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} and the family had a falling-out last year, and it has not healed.
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} cut off the family some months ago.
entry: Stopped speaking to the family a while ago (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Did not open the door to a parent, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Fell out with the family last year, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: A small wrapped gift on a step
storylets.note: A gift is handed over at a door. The giver is named only if someone says so.

b1: {A} comes up to {place} with a small wrapped package behind {A.his} back.
{A} arrives at the door with a wrapped package and straightens a crooked ribbon.
{A} comes up to the door holding a flat parcel tied in string.
b2: The door of {place} slides open. {A} hands the parcel to {B.desc} with both hands.
{A} holds out the package. {B.desc} turns it over twice, grinning.
{A} says something and hands the wrapped parcel across.
b3: {B.desc} pulls {A} into a hug and the parcel is crushed between them.
{A} and {B.desc} hug in the doorway, laughing.
{B.desc} embraces {A}, then steps back and tears the wrapping open.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Happy birthday. One more year on you."
Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Another year, and you still wrap presents like a kid. I love it."
